q: Under SA 210, which of the following is a precondition for an audit that the auditor must establish BEFORE accepting the engagement?
o: The entity maintains an internal audit function as required by section 138
An acceptable reporting framework and management acknowledging its responsibility
The predecessor auditor has issued a no objection certificate to the incoming firm
The audit fee has been approved by the shareholders at the annual general meeting
why: SA 210 preconditions are two: the use of an acceptable financial reporting framework, and management acknowledging its responsibility for the financial statements, internal control and providing access. A no objection certificate and fee approval are professional or statutory matters, not SA 210 preconditions.

q: What is the key distinction between the overall audit strategy and the audit plan under SA 300?
o: The strategy is prepared by the engagement partner and the plan by the client
The strategy sets scope, timing and direction; the plan sets nature and extent
The strategy is documented after fieldwork closes and the plan is set before it
They are the same document and the two terms are used interchangeably here
why: SA 300 says the overall audit strategy sets the scope, timing and direction of the audit and guides development of the audit plan. The audit plan is more detailed, covering the nature, timing and extent of planned risk assessment and further audit procedures.

q: Which of these is NOT a risk assessment procedure under SA 315?
o: Inquiries of management and of others within the entity who hold information
Analytical procedures applied to financial and non financial data at planning
Observation of entity processes and inspection of documents and of records
External confirmation of trade receivable balances obtained from customers
why: SA 315 lists exactly three risk assessment procedures: inquiry, analytical procedures, and observation and inspection. External confirmation is a substantive procedure under SA 505, performed as a further audit procedure, not to assess risk.

q: As the assessed risk of material misstatement increases, how should the auditor ordinarily change the timing of substantive procedures?
o: Shift more of the work to an interim date so effort is spread across the year
Shift more of the work to a date at or near the period end of the entity
Timing is not affected by risk because only the extent of testing changes
Complete all substantive procedures before the interim date is reached
why: Higher risk pushes procedures closer to period end, because testing at an interim date leaves a remaining period that must be covered by additional roll forward procedures. Lower risk permits more interim testing.

q: Under SA 500, the sufficiency and the appropriateness of audit evidence refer respectively to:
o: The quality of the evidence and then the quantity of the evidence obtained
The quantity of the evidence and then the quality of the evidence obtained
The relevance of the evidence and then the reliability of that evidence
The cost of obtaining the evidence and the timing of when it was obtained
why: Sufficiency is the measure of the quantity of audit evidence. Appropriateness is the measure of its quality, that is its relevance and reliability. Higher quality can reduce the quantity needed, but poor quality evidence cannot be cured by obtaining more of it.

q: On an initial audit engagement, SA 510 requires the auditor to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence about whether:
o: The predecessor auditor issued an unmodified opinion on the preceding period
Opening balances contain misstatements that materially affect the period
The preceding period audit was conducted under the same reporting framework
The entity has changed its accounting software during the preceding period
why: SA 510 focuses on whether opening balances contain misstatements materially affecting the current period, and whether appropriate accounting policies reflected in opening balances have been consistently applied. The prior opinion is relevant information but not the objective itself.

q: An auditor signs the report on 20 May. On 28 May, before the statements are issued, a material subsequent event is identified and management amends the accounts. If procedures are extended only to that event, the correct approach is:
o: Withdraw the original report and re date the entire report to 28 May
Use dual dating, keeping the original date and adding one for the change
Issue a fresh report dated 28 May covering all subsequent events afresh
Add an emphasis of matter paragraph and retain the original report date
why: Dual dating limits the auditor responsibility for subsequent events to the specific amendment. Re dating the whole report would extend responsibility for all subsequent events up to the new date, requiring full procedures to that date.

q: Under SA 570, the auditor evaluates the management assessment of going concern covering a period of:
o: At least six months measured from the balance sheet date of the entity
At least twelve months measured from the balance sheet date of the entity
At least twelve months measured from the date of the auditor report
Three years, matching the business plan that the board has approved
why: SA 570 requires management assessment to cover a period of at least twelve months from the balance sheet date. If management assessment covers less than that, the auditor asks management to extend it.

q: Written representations under SA 580 should be dated:
o: On the balance sheet date of the period covered by the financial statements
As near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor report
At least thirty days before the date on which the auditor report is signed
On the date the audit fieldwork commenced at the premises of the entity
why: SA 580 requires written representations to be dated as near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor report, so that they cover the whole period on which the auditor is reporting.

q: Under SA 230, the final audit file should ordinarily be assembled within:
o: Thirty days after the date of the auditor report on the financial statements
Sixty days after the date of the auditor report on the statements
Ninety days after the balance sheet date of the period being reported on
Before the auditor report on the financial statements is finally signed
why: SA 230 sets an administrative assembly period ordinarily not more than 60 days after the date of the auditor report. Under SQC 1, working papers are then retained for at least seven years.

q: Which statement about professional skepticism is MOST accurate?
o: It requires the auditor to begin from an assumption that management is dishonest
It means assuming neither dishonesty nor unquestioned honesty by management
It becomes applicable only once a specific fraud risk has been identified
It may be relaxed where the auditor has a long standing client relationship
why: Professional skepticism means a questioning mind and a critical assessment of audit evidence. SA 200 makes clear the auditor neither assumes dishonesty nor unquestioned honesty, and a long client relationship does not justify reducing skepticism.

q: An auditor decides NOT to rely on internal controls for the revenue cycle. The consequence is that the auditor:
o: Is relieved of any need to understand the revenue process of the entity
Must still perform tests of controls in order to confirm that decision
Adopts a fully substantive approach with increased substantive testing
Must issue a qualified opinion on the internal financial controls
why: Understanding the process is mandatory under SA 315 regardless. If the auditor does not plan to rely on controls, tests of controls are not required, but substantive procedures must be sufficiently extensive to reduce detection risk on their own.

q: Under SA 265, significant deficiencies in internal control identified during the audit must be communicated to those charged with governance:
o: Orally, at the closing meeting that is held with the audit committee
In writing, and on a timely basis during or shortly after the audit
Only where management has refused to remediate the deficiency found
Only in the case of listed companies and their material subsidiaries
why: SA 265 requires significant deficiencies to be communicated in writing and on a timely basis to those charged with governance. Other, less significant deficiencies may be communicated to management orally.

q: Detection risk is BEST described as:
o: A risk arising from the entity that the auditor is unable to influence
The risk that internal controls fail to prevent or detect a misstatement
The risk that the procedures of the auditor fail to detect a misstatement
The same as inherent risk for balances involving significant judgement
why: Detection risk is the risk that the auditor procedures will not detect a material misstatement that exists. It is the only component of audit risk the auditor directly controls, by varying the nature, timing and extent of procedures.

q: In an audit where inherent risk and control risk are both assessed as high, the auditor should set detection risk:
o: High, so that the overall audit risk model is kept in balance
Low, and therefore perform more persuasive audit procedures
At a level that is equal to the assessed level of control risk
Detection risk is fixed in advance by the methodology of the firm
why: Audit risk is held at an acceptably low level. If inherent and control risk are high, detection risk must be driven low, which means more persuasive evidence, larger samples and period end rather than interim testing.

q: Which of the following BEST describes the responsibility of the auditor for the financial statements?
o: To prepare and to present the financial statements of the entity fairly
To express an opinion on whether they give a true and fair view
To guarantee that the statements are free from any misstatement
To certify the accuracy of every single transaction that was recorded
why: Preparation and fair presentation is management responsibility. The auditor expresses an opinion, obtaining reasonable, not absolute, assurance. An audit is not a guarantee or a certification of every transaction.
